part.text: The file covers complete calendar years through 2025, then only part of 2026. Brooklyn pedestrian injury counts fell between 2013 and 2025, while pedestrian deaths rose; I’m charting those separately so the two severity measures don’t mask each other. These are victim counts, not risk rates, since the file has no measure of how much people walked.

+import json
+import os
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+DATA = "data/crashes.parquet"
+OUT = "out"
+os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
+
+con = duckdb.connect()
+annual = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
+           count(*) AS brooklyn_crash_rows,
+           count(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_pedestrians_injured IS NULL)
+               AS null_injury_rows,
+           count(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_pedestrians_killed IS NULL)
+               AS null_fatality_rows,
+           sum(number_of_pedestrians_injured) AS pedestrians_injured,
+           sum(number_of_pedestrians_killed) AS pedestrians_killed
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN'
+      AND crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY 1
+    ORDER BY 1
+    """,
+    [DATA],
+).df()
+
+coverage = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year, min(crash_date) AS first_date,
+           max(crash_date) AS last_date, count(*) AS borough_null_rows,
+           count(*) FILTER (WHERE borough IS NULL) * 100.0 / count(*)
+               AS borough_null_pct
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025
+    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
+    """,
+    [DATA],
+).df()
+null_summary = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT count(*) AS total_rows,
+           count(*) FILTER (WHERE borough IS NULL) AS null_borough_rows,
+           count(*) FILTER (WHERE borough IS NULL) * 100.0 / count(*)
+               AS null_borough_pct
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025
+    """,
+    [DATA],
+).df().iloc[0]
+excluded_years = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year, count(*) AS brooklyn_crash_rows,
+           min(crash_date) AS first_date, max(crash_date) AS last_date
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN' AND year(crash_date) IN (2012, 2026)
+    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
+    """,
+    [DATA],
+).df()
+
+years = annual["year"].astype(int).tolist()
+assert years == list(range(2013, 2026))
+assert annual["null_injury_rows"].sum() == 0
+assert annual["null_fatality_rows"].sum() == 0
+
+plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "axes.spines.top": False,
+                     "axes.spines.right": False})
+
+
+def make_chart(column, ylabel, title, subtitle, color, filename, value_format):
+    values = annual[column].astype(int)
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.8, 6.0), constrained_layout=True)
+    ax.plot(years, values, color=color, linewidth=3, marker="o",
+            markersize=6, markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1.3)
+    ax.fill_between(years, values, 0, color=color, alpha=0.10)
+    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=19, fontweight="bold", pad=30)
+    ax.text(0, 1.015, subtitle, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=10.5,
+            color="#4b5563", va="bottom")
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, fontsize=11, labelpad=10)
+    ax.set_xlabel("Calendar year", fontsize=11, labelpad=10)
+    ax.set_xticks(years)
+    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=45, labelsize=9)
+    ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=10)
+    ax.grid(axis="y", color="#d9dee7", linewidth=0.8)
+    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+    ax.set_ylim(bottom=0, top=max(values) * 1.20)
+    for idx in (0, len(years) - 1):
+        ax.annotate(value_format.format(int(values.iloc[idx])),
+                    (years[idx], values.iloc[idx]),
+                    xytext=(0, 11 if idx == 0 else 13),
+                    textcoords="offset points", ha="center",
+                    fontsize=10, fontweight="bold", color=color)
+    fig.text(0.01, -0.015,
+             "Source: NYC police-reported motor-vehicle crashes. Counts are victims, not rates per walking trip.",
+             fontsize=8.5, color="#4b5563")
+    fig.savefig(os.path.join(OUT, filename), dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+
+make_chart(
+    "pedestrians_injured", "Pedestrian injury victims", 
+    "Brooklyn pedestrian injuries fell from 2013, then climbed",
+    "Annual victims in police-reported motor-vehicle crashes · complete years only",
+    "#1769aa", "option_1.png", "{:,}",
+)
+make_chart(
+    "pedestrians_killed", "Pedestrian deaths", 
+    "Brooklyn pedestrian deaths fluctuate—and were higher in 2025",
+    "Annual victims in police-reported motor-vehicle crashes · complete years only",
+    "#b33a3a", "option_2.png", "{}",

+injury_end = int(annual.loc[annual.year == 2025, "pedestrians_injured"].iloc[0])
